signals.signal: HARD FLEET NUMBER, never previously captured: Alpha Bank operated 1,199 ATMs in Greece at 31/12/2025 — 575 on-site (252 Attica, 50 Thessaloniki, 273 rest of Greece) and 624 OFF-SITE (231 Attica, 54 Thessaloniki, 339 rest of Greece). Off-site devices are 52% of the fleet, outnumbering on-site. Greek market total across HBA member banks was 5,625 ATMs; Alpha is third-largest by fleet behind Piraeus (1,641) and NBG (1,360) and marginally behind Eurobank (1,237).
signals.source_name: Hellenic Bank Association — 'A.T.M. Network of the HBA Member Banks', per-bank data as of 31/12/2025
signals.implies: Sizes the entire Printec addressable estate at Alpha for the first time. The 52% off-site share is the commercially important half: off-site ATMs carry the cash-in-transit cost, the remote-monitoring load and the availability risk, which is exactly the managed-services and remote-diagnostics pitch. It also gives a denominator against which the H1-2026 'ten new off-site ATMs' and the 97.5% availability KPI can be priced.
signals.likelihood: Certain — published per-bank by the banks' own association
signals.followup: Build the Alpha fleet-refresh proposal off 1,199 units with 624 off-site; ask what share is deposit/recycling-capable, and reconcile the 31/12/2025 base against the H1-2026 net additions. Re-pull this HBA PDF each year — a changed count is itself the signal.

signals.signal: Contactless (NFC) ATM rollout COMPLETED across the entire ATM network in January 2026; adoption already reached 30% of total ATM transactions. Network availability 97.5% in H1-2026, up 0.5 percentage points YoY. 137 ATM network optimisation studies were completed in H1-2026, resulting in the installation of ten new off-site ATMs. ATM transaction volumes remained stable over the period. Self-service banking devices are described as 'the primary transaction channel within the Bank's branch network'.
signals.source_name: Alpha Bank — Semi Annual Financial Report H1-2026, Board of Directors' Semi Annual Management Report, section 'ATM Network & Automated Payment Systems'
signals.implies: Fleet-wide contactless is DONE, so the next spend cycle moves off card-reader retrofit and onto fleet refresh, cash automation/recyclers and availability-driven managed services. A published 97.5% availability figure with a stated improvement trend is an explicit SLA conversation. 137 optimisation studies producing only ten net new off-site machines signals active site rationalisation — redeployment and refresh rather than expansion, which is the higher-margin Printec motion.
signals.likelihood: Very likely — a live, funded programme with a published availability KPI and an annual optimisation cycle
signals.followup: Ask Alpha's Self-Service Banking owner for the FY-2027 refresh envelope and whether the 137-study cycle repeats in H2-2026; pitch availability uplift beyond 97.5% as a managed-service SLA, and recyclers for the off-site estate.

signals.signal: 98% of the Bank's branch network is equipped with at least one Automated Payment System (APS), enabling customers to perform deposits and payments unaided. Alpha explicitly defines its digital channels as 'Web, Mobile, ATM, APS' — and those channels carried 98% of total monetary transaction volume in H1-2026, leaving only 2% at the branch counter. Digital banking transactions rose 8.7% in volume and 11% in value versus 2025. The live APS product page (checked 27/08/2026) confirms these are full cash-accepting devices: they take BANKNOTES AND COINS, offer four identification routes (card in slot, card number keyed, contactless tap, or cash), scan bill barcodes, accept credit-card payments for cards issued by OTHER Greek banks, and credit Alpha accounts immediately.
signals.source_name: Alpha Bank — Semi Annual Financial Report H1-2026, Digital Banking section and monetary-transactions channel-mix chart
signals.implies: Alpha classifies ATM and APS as digital channels alongside web and mobile — the self-service estate is strategic, not legacy, which changes how it is budgeted. With only 2% of monetary transactions left at the counter, residual cash workload must be absorbed by machines: the textbook case for recyclers and higher-capacity deposit automation, plus managed services to hold availability as volume concentrates on fewer devices. Coin handling is the detail worth noting — coin-accepting units are a distinct, maintenance-heavy device class, which strengthens the recurring-service argument alongside the hardware one.
signals.likelihood: Very likely — the channel shift has already happened; the open question is device capability, not strategy
signals.followup: Quantify how many APS units are deposit/recycling-capable versus payment-only, and pitch recyclers against the 2% counter-cash residual — the same white-space analysis Printec ran on the Bulgarian fleets.

signals.signal: Branch and headcount base, from two independent primary sources: HBA per-bank data gives Alpha 249 branches in Greece and 5,665 personnel at 31/12/2025 (Greek market: 1,291 branches, 27,351 personnel). Alpha's own Q2-2026 investor deck shows 261 branches (a series falling 443 -> 261 since Dec-2018, footnoted as including corporate and private banking centres) and 5,754 employees in Greece at 30/06/2026. Combined with the 1,199-ATM fleet, that is roughly 4.8 ATMs per branch.
signals.source_name: Hellenic Bank Association — 'Branch Network Data and Number of Personnel of the HBA Members', 31/12/2025; and Alpha Bank Q2-2026 Results Investor Presentation
signals.implies: SUPERSEDES the baseline's '245 branches' scraped from the alpha.gr website, and reconciles the country figure against the bank's own disclosure — the reconciliation the baseline flagged as never having been done. The branch series has flattened (262/261/261/261 across the last four quarters), so Alpha is NOT closing branches: like CEC Bank in Romania, the play is automation INSIDE a retained network. That is the cash-automation argument, not a decommissioning one.
signals.likelihood: Certain — two independent primary disclosures agree once definitions are aligned
signals.followup: Use the flat branch count plus the falling headcount as the core pitch: same estate, fewer staff, so the machines have to take the load. Track whether the 261 series breaks downward at the November Investor Day.

signals.signal: NEW voluntary separation scheme in CYPRUS: Euro 17.5m provision booked in Q2-2026 (Euro 18m at group adjusted-profit level). CFO Vassilios Kosmas on the results call: it is 'primarily the envisaged restructuring charge for the acquisition of AstroBank'. Total H1-2026 provisions of Euro 77m (vs Euro 6m in H1-2025) include Euro 64m for new voluntary separation schemes for employees in Greece AND Cyprus — the Greek leg being the Euro 47m / c.350 FTE round provisioned in Q1-2026. Q2-2026 also carried Euro 1.4m of Cyprus integration costs, and group G&A rose on 'higher IT expenses, partly attributable to the integration of AstroBank's systems into Alpha Bank Cyprus'.
signals.source_name: Alpha Bank — Semi Annual Financial Report H1-2026 (provisions note) and Q2-2026 Results Investor Presentation (footnote to normalisation bridge)
signals.implies: CORRECTS the baseline, which recorded the Feb-2026 VSS as closed with no new round. There IS a fresh round, in Cyprus, and it is explicitly the AstroBank restructuring charge — meaning branch consolidation and system unification in Cyprus are being funded now. Staff leaving cash-handling roles during a two-bank merger is the strongest single trigger for recyclers, APS and self-service migration, and the AstroBank systems integration is simultaneously an open IT-integration workstream.
signals.likelihood: Very likely — the provision is booked, so the departures and the integration execute across H2-2026
signals.followup: Get the headcount and branch-role split behind the Euro 17.5m Cyprus charge, and the combined Alpha Cyprus + ex-AstroBank branch and ATM overlap map — duplicate sites are where recyclers and redeployed machines land.

signals.signal: Investor Day scheduled for NOVEMBER 2026, at which CEO Vassilios Psaltis says the Bank will present its business model and value creation for the coming years in detail — the successor to the 2023-2026 Strategic Plan, whose completion Euromoney already marked in July 2026. Announced alongside upgraded guidance: FY-2026 EPS revised UP to Euro 0.41 (+13% growth), H1-2026 profit after tax Euro 497.2m (normalised Euro 495.3m), RoTBV 14% for H1 and 15.5% in Q2, CET1 14.3%, cost-to-income 38%, NPE ratio 3.6%. A Euro 273m H1 distribution provision and an interim dividend of c.Euro 124m in Q4 are planned, plus a buyback of up to 205,000,000 shares (9.1% of capital) which began executing on 14/08/2026.
signals.source_name: Alpha Bank — Q2/H1 2026 results press release (CEO statement) and Own Shares Buyback Programme announcements
signals.implies: The next multi-year capex envelope — including whatever is set aside for the branch estate, self-service and technology — gets fixed at the November Investor Day. That is the window in which to be positioned, not afterwards. Guidance was raised and capital is being returned, so the funding capacity is demonstrably there; the constraint is priority, not money.
signals.likelihood: Certain — the date is publicly committed by the CEO and repeated on the analyst call
signals.followup: Diarise November 2026. Brief Alpha's self-service and transformation owners BEFORE the plan locks, and read the deck the day it drops for any stated branch or ATM estate target.

signals.signal: New International Customer Onboarding service launched in H1-2026: individuals resident in Germany, the United Kingdom, the United States, Cyprus and Israel can open a deposit account, obtain a debit card and gain e-Banking access entirely remotely, without visiting a branch in Greece, with 'plans for gradual expansion to additional countries'. Domestically, 31% of new accounts were opened through the Retail On Boarding service in myAlpha Mobile; online debit-card issuance reached 36% of issuance and new credit-card digital issuance 35%; 31% of all retail products were sold digitally and 80% of consumer loans disbursed via digital channels.
signals.source_name: Alpha Bank — Semi Annual Financial Report H1-2026, Digital Banking and Digital Sales sections
signals.implies: Cross-border remote account opening is the hardest eKYC case there is: non-resident identity proofing across five different document regimes, sanctions and PEP screening at onboarding, and liveness/anti-deepfake checks. A stated roadmap to add countries means recurring incremental eKYC scope rather than a one-off build. Directly Printec's digital onboarding/eKYC line, and it drags AML screening in behind it.
signals.likelihood: Likely — the service is live and further expansion is stated policy
signals.followup: Identify which identity-verification and liveness vendor Alpha uses for the non-resident flow, and which countries are next in the expansion queue.

signals.entity: Alpha Bank / AMLA / Bank of Greece
signals.signal: AMLA — the EU Anti-Money Laundering Authority, which took over the EBA's AML functions on 31/12/2025 — ran a data collection and testing exercise through H1-2026 to calibrate the risk-assessment models that will select up to 40 entities for AMLA DIRECT supervision: selection in 2027, supervision starting 2028. AMLA announced the exercise 26/01/2026 and published the reporting package 16/03/2026. The Bank of Greece launched a group-level data collection exercise on 15/06/2026 to identify Greek obliged entities and groups meeting the eligibility criteria. Alpha Bank participated in AMLA's public hearings and consultations — including draft RTS on Customer Due Diligence, draft Guidelines on Ongoing Monitoring of a Business Relationship, and draft Guidelines on Business-Wide Risk Assessment — via the Hellenic Banking Association.
signals.source_name: Alpha Bank — Semi Annual Financial Report H1-2026, section 'Regulatory environment for anti-money laundering and financial sectors' digital transformation'
signals.implies: A dated regulatory clock on AML and transaction-monitoring spend. If Alpha lands in AMLA's direct-supervision cohort, its CDD, ongoing-monitoring and business-wide-risk-assessment tooling faces a step change in scrutiny from 2028, with selection decided in 2027 — so remediation budget has to be committed across 2026-2027, i.e. now. This is the sharpest available hook for the AML/transaction-monitoring line and for screening at onboarding, and it reinforces the Bank of Greece's 2025 enforcement findings on transaction-monitoring shortcomings that the previous run logged.
signals.likelihood: Likely — the Bank of Greece has already collected the group-level data and Alpha is among the largest Greek groups, so a plausible candidate
signals.followup: Track the AMLA 2027 selection list and the outcome of the Bank of Greece 15/06/2026 data collection; approach Alpha's AML/Compliance owner now on ongoing-monitoring and BWRA tooling gaps measured against the draft RTS.

signals.signal: Alpha Bank abolished the foreign-exchange conversion fee on the entire Aegean Bonus Visa card family from 25/08/2026 — the previous 2% FX conversion fee on non-euro transactions drops to 0%, with no time limit, no amount cap and no conditions, applied automatically to existing and new debit, credit and Premium cards. Separately, Alpha is in the middle of replacing its Mastercard cards with Visa cards (confirmed on the live alpha.gr cards pages).
signals.source_name: Alpha Bank — press release, 'Alpha Bank fully abolishes the FX conversion fee on Aegean Bonus Visa cards'
signals.implies: Two adjacent effects. First, Alpha's ATMs run Dynamic Currency Conversion on foreign-currency cards, so the economics of FX at the terminal are actively being repriced — worth checking whether the DCC configuration on the fleet changes with it. Second, a full Mastercard-to-Visa card portfolio migration is a large issuing, key-management and HSM workload, and re-issuance at that scale touches card personalisation and ATM card-management functions.
signals.likelihood: Likely — the fee change is already live; the scheme migration is confirmed and in progress
signals.followup: Confirm the scale and timetable of the Mastercard-to-Visa reissuance and whether DCC settings across the 1,199-ATM fleet are being reconfigured alongside the fee change.

signals.signal: Executive Committee reshuffle announced 30/07/2026: Iosif Kiouroukoglou becomes Chief of Wholesale Banking and an ExCo member reporting directly to the Group CEO from 15/09/2026, succeeding Yannis Emiris (in post since 2019); Chief Wealth Management Officer Giorgos Michalopoulos also moves to a direct CEO reporting line. Separately, the Alpha Trust squeeze-out completed 24/08/2026, taking Alpha to 100% of Alpha Trust Holdings at Euro 20.20 per share, and the buyback of up to 205,000,000 shares (9.1% of capital) began executing 14/08/2026.
signals.source_name: Alpha Bank — press release of 30/07/2026 and corporate announcements of 24/08/2026
signals.implies: New buying-centre map ahead of the November Investor Day: a new wholesale owner takes office 15/09/2026, which is the window in which incoming executives set their own vendor agenda. Full ownership of Alpha Trust also removes the minority constraint on consolidating the wealth platform — the H1 report confirms a unified advisory platform is being designed and built.
signals.likelihood: Certain for the appointments; the platform consolidation is disclosed as in progress
signals.followup: Re-map Alpha's decision makers after 15/09/2026 and get in front of the incoming Chief of Wholesale Banking before the November Investor Day.

signals.signal: LIVE DEADLINE, re-verified against the primary press release: FinQuest 2026 applications remain open until 20/09/2026 (an extension of the original window). Two of the competition's themes sit squarely on Printec's ground — 'Fraud Zero & Digital Trust' (fraud-protection technologies, cybersecurity, digital identity) and a customer-experience theme naming digital onboarding explicitly — with AI as the stated centrepiece this year. Winners receive a pilot in Alpha's real banking environment, and finalists gain direct access to Alpha business and technology decision makers.
signals.source_name: Alpha Bank — press release, 'FinQuest 2026: extension to 20 September for applications to this year's innovation competition'
signals.implies: A named, dated, open door into Alpha's fraud, digital-identity, eKYC and AML buying centre, closing in under a month. The value is less the prize than the structured access to decision makers and the pilot slot in a production banking environment — a route into the account that bypasses procurement. Carried from the previous run because the deadline is still live and now imminent.
signals.followup: Decide before 20/09/2026 whether Printec or a partner startup enters the Fraud Zero & Digital Trust or digital-onboarding theme; at minimum, use the FinQuest cycle to map who at Alpha judges it.

signals.signal: GAP, reported as a negative finding: no Alpha Bank disclosure and no located public source names Siron, FICO/Tonbeller or any other AML transaction-monitoring vendor at Alpha Bank. The H1-2026 Semi Annual Financial Report covers the AML regulatory agenda at length (AMLA RTS/ITS/Guidelines, the 20th EU sanctions package of 23/04/2026, DORA implementation) and names no supplier anywhere. Targeted searching in English and Greek returned only generic FICO Siron product material, none of it referencing Alpha.
signals.source_name: Alpha Bank — Semi Annual Financial Report H1-2026 (negative finding, whole-document check) plus targeted English/Greek web search
signals.implies: The 'Siron AML partner' premise in the tasking is UNVERIFIED and must not be carried forward as fact — most likely it refers to Printec's own regional Siron reseller relationship rather than to a confirmed deployment at Alpha. Commercially this is good news rather than bad: Alpha's AML stack is undisclosed, so it is contestable, and the AMLA 2027/2028 clock supplies the reason to open the conversation.
signals.followup: Establish through Printec's own account team whether a Siron relationship exists at Alpha; if it does, it is not publicly disclosed anywhere and should be sourced internally rather than cited.

signals.signal: Re-verified from the live alpha.gr ATM page (checked 27/08/2026): Alpha ATMs support contactless transactions using either a card or a digital wallet (phone/smartwatch); cash deposits to own or third-party Alpha accounts credited immediately on completion; Dynamic Currency Conversion with the rate shown during the transaction for foreign-currency cards; card activation and PIN change; prepaid card load in cash or by transfer; balance and last-10-transactions printing; and acceptance of cards issued by other banks in Greece and abroad. Strategic framing re-verified: 25 geographical Regions established March 2026, Chief Retail Distribution Officer reporting directly to the CEO since July 2025, branches moving from transaction points to advisory and development centres.
signals.source_name: Alpha Bank — ATM services page (retail support centre), cross-checked against the H1-2026 Semi Annual Financial Report Retail Banking transformation section
signals.implies: Confirms the functional envelope Printec would be extending rather than replacing: the fleet already does contactless, immediate-credit deposit and DCC. The remaining capability gaps to sell against are recycling (cash reuse rather than deposit-only), higher-denomination and bulk note handling, and the availability/monitoring layer — not basic feature parity.
signals.likelihood: Certain — verified on the live primary page this run
signals.followup: Establish what share of the 1,199 machines are true recyclers versus deposit-only, since the public page does not distinguish them.

coverage_notes: Fresh full run; no checkpoint existed for 2026-08-27. The 30/07 run stopped one day before Alpha's H1-2026 results (31/07/2026), so the entire August reporting cluster was unexamined. Primary sources opened this run: the alpha.gr Greek press-office index and full press-release list (desktop UA), the Q2/H1-2026 results press release, the Q2-2026 investor presentation deck, the H1-2026 English Semi Annual Financial Report (4.4MB), all nine corporate announcements dated 30/07-25/08/2026, the live alpha.gr ATM page, and the Alpha Bank Cyprus ex-AstroBank pages. NEW SOURCE ENVIRONMENT introduced this run: the Hellenic Bank Association per-bank statistics series (hba.gr/En/Statistics/List), which publishes bank-by-bank ATM fleet and branch/personnel PDFs — never used by any previous run, and the source of the first hard Alpha ATM fleet count (1,199) and the country-vs-bank reconciliation the baseline flagged as outstanding. All PDF text extracted locally with pypdf. Genuine gap: no AML vendor (Siron or otherwise) is named in any Alpha disclosure or public source — reported as an explicit negative finding rather than dropped. Alpha is a private issuer, so public procurement registers (Diavgeia, KIMDIS, TED) carry no Alpha tenders and were not a productive route.
